cases.name: Erika Andrea Gaytan
cases.narrative:
Gaytan was last seen on the evening of July 13 after attending a concert at the El Paso County Coliseum with Marquez. He had claimed they parted ways later that night and Gaytan reportedly called an Uber. But the affidavit claims Marquez actually drove Gaytan to his home in the 3600 block of Nehemiah, where they argued and he killed her. The document indicated police seized a Jeep belonging to Marquez's family that contained Gaytan's blood in it; he allegedly transported her body in the rear cargo section of the vehicle to a desert area off East Montana where detectives believe he buried her using a shovel that they've also recovered. In addition, the affidavit said police also found zip ties and sand-filled shoes during a search of Marquez's home. Authorities believe both of those items are also linked to Gaytan's death.

cases.name: Dafne Michelle Davila
cases.about: Her obituary called her "a beacon of love and laughter." It said: "Born ... in Mexico, Dafne was a cherished daughter, sister, and friend whose vibrant spirit and kind heart left an indelible mark on all who knew her. Dafne grew up in a close-knit family, where she was deeply loved by her mother, Irma Gonzalez, and was a source of endless joy to her sister, Tania Rodriguez, and her brother, Juan Carlos Rodriguez Caldera. She was preceded by her father, Jesus Oscar Davila, whose memory she held dear to her heart. Dafne followed her passion for beauty and creativity by pursuing a career in cosmetology. Her natural talent and dedication to her craft earned her a respected place in the industry as a hairstylist. Dafne’s clients didn't just see her for her skills with scissors and hair dye; they came for the warmth and care that she infused into every appointment. She had a unique ability to make every person who sat in her chair feel special and seen. Dafne's infectious laugh and playful demeanor were complemented by a profound kindness that she extended to everyone she met. She was the kind of person who brought light into the room, and her sense of humor was a gift that she generously shared, lifting spirits and spreading happiness. As we remember Dafne, we celebrate the love she gave so freely and the memories she created with us. Her legacy of kindness and joy will continue to inspire those who were fortunate enough to have known her. Her family takes comfort in the fact that her loving spirit will live on through the countless lives she touched. Dafne Michelle Davila's life was a testament to the beauty that can be created when one leads with love and laughter. Though her time with us was too short, the impact she made will endure. She will be profoundly missed by her family, friends, and all who were graced by her presence."
cases.narrative:
Responding to a 911 call. a deputy went inside the home and saw Dafne on the floor kitchen with large amounts of blood and a knife in her throat.She was gasping for air and appeared to be conscious, but she died at the hospital.

The 911 calls depict Davila requesting help, saying Chavez had assaulted her with his fists. She also told dispatchers she was hiding in the last room of the home. She again pleaded for help to dispatch, saying her boyfriend, Chavez, was breaking down the door of her room. Shortly after Davila screams, Chavez's voice can be heard in the 911 call, according to the document. Loud thuds can be heard, such as an assault and then sounds of gasping and labored breathing were heard.
